audit.why: 53.19% over 673 games, EVEN at 5.5/10, is consistent with the kits: Lux outranges Breath of Light (750) with E (1100) and Q (1175) all lane, and loses only to a fully stacked Aurelion Sol late.
audit.corrected: Early and mid lane favour Lux; side lane and late teamfights favour Aurelion Sol once Stardust accumulates.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[3..5].side read 'Skill' while content win[3..5] read 'Lux' and the packet levelChart reads Lux for rows 0-5. The page rendered two answers for Levels 4-5, Level 6 and First item.
audit.why: Nothing in either kit flips those stages: Asol has no kill threat before Stardust, his Falling Star is 120s at rank 1 against Lux's 60s Final Spark, and Lux's burst leads until he stacks.
audit.corrected: phases[3].side, phases[4].side and phases[5].side set to 'Lux' to match win[3..5] and the packet chart; each why rewritten in the same group to justify the verdict. win[N] already reads 'Lux' so no content edit is proposed (a no-op would be rejected).

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: both Breath of Light (Q) and Astral Flight (W) are channels, and Light Binding cancels them outright. Singularity (E) was also unstated as a percent-health execute inside a 750-range pull.
audit.why: The kit flags mark Q and W as interruptible channels and E as percentHealth + execute + zone. These are the whole matchup and the page instead carried generic 'track Astral Flight' template text.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, breakdown.carry, dosFull[0].d and dontsFull[2].d now carry the channel-cancel, the 12s/750 black hole with its execute threshold, and the real Astral Flight cooldown band (22s rank 1 to 16s rank 5).

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1].text named 'Cosmic Rupture', which is not an Aurelion Sol ability.
audit.why: Riot's kit lists R as Falling Star, upgrading to The Skies Descend at enough Stardust. 'Cosmic Rupture' is a fabrication; the packet flagged it against the passive name Cosmic Creator, but the correct fix is The Skies Descend.
audit.corrected: Replaced with Falling Star / The Skies Descend plus the real 120s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the field that holds real cooldowns and it carried only prose.
audit.corrected: Now states Astral Flight 22s -> 16s, Singularity 12s flat, and the Light Binding channel cancel.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, both under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: The title promised the passive weave and the R discipline; the bodies explained trading.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their own titles, grounded in Illumination's detonation and Final Spark's 60s rank-1 cooldown.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — E every wave contact. Bank Manaflow and hold Q for his aggression, not yours.
edits.after: Lost Chapter timing — E every wave contact so he farms Breath of Light under tower and his Stardust stalls.

edits.before: Final Spark online — anything the root catches dies to the laser math. The lane becomes a geometry quiz.
edits.after: Final Spark online — his Falling Star is 120s and telegraphed, yours is 60s. You still win the level 6 trade.

edits.before: Luden's spike: Q-E-R deletes squishies from root range. Force him to dodge or die on every contact.
edits.after: Luden's spike: Q-E-R deletes him from 1175 before he is stacked — force the dodge on every contact.

edits.before: - Aurelion Sol Astral Flight: matchup-defining — His reposition and escape — he is a stationary battery while it is down. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your W Prismatic Barrier like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Astral Flight: 22s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5 — his only reposition, and he is a stationary battery for that whole window. - Singularity is 12s flat and executes below a percent threshold — stay above it. - Light Binding cancels either channel outright.

edits.before: His reposition and escape — he is a stationary battery while it is down. Its cooldown is the green light — wait for it.
edits.after: Singularity is 750 range and 12s; your E outranges it at 1100, so drop it on his last-hit spot and never stand in the pull.

edits.before: E the contact, detonate, weave the passive auto, and keep Q visibly loaded — the chip is free and the root threat does the zoning.
edits.after: Illumination arms on any spell hit and your auto detonates it — Q or E, then step in for the auto, then back out of his 750 breath range.

edits.before: Aurelion Sol burns Astral Flight on nothing — take the fifteen-second invitation.
edits.after: Aurelion Sol burns Astral Flight on nothing — that is 22 seconds without an escape.

edits.before: Q-poking on cooldown and facing the dive with an empty root slot — Lux without the binding banked is everyone's favorite snack.
edits.after: Final Spark is 60s at rank 1 and it is your answer to his R engage — a wave cleared with it costs you the fight forty seconds later.

edits.before: Aurelion Sol wins by landing Astral Flight, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Aurelion Sol wins by stacking Stardust until Breath of Light outgrows your poke and Singularity executes you.

edits.before: Carry through the root-laser pipeline — one binding per fight, converted at screen range; your job is owning the geometry that makes it land.
edits.after: Carry by cancelling him: Light Binding interrupts Breath of Light and Astral Flight mid-cast, killing his damage and his exit in one root.

edits.before: If Aurelion Sol gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Astral Flight extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with E clears and stay relevant through root picks.
edits.after: A kill feeds Stardust as well as gold, so it compounds — stand outside 750 and never contest a wave he is breathing. Two kills: farm from E range only, and let your jungler take the black hole, not you.

edits.before: Ahead, own the geometry: E Aurelion Sol off every contact, root the answers, and laser the river fights from fog — fed Lux turns vision lines into kill lines.
edits.after: Ahead, deny Stardust: shove every wave so he takes it under tower, root him off the black hole, and laser him out of Astral Flight range before he lands.

edits.before: You still hold the edge at 6: his R (Falling Star/Cosmic Rupture) is a long telegraphed slam, easy to sidestep, and it doesn't give him a kill on you through your shield. Keep poking and denying his stacks, since every level you keep him behind delays his only win condition.
edits.after: You still hold the edge at 6: his R (Falling Star) is a telegraphed slam on a 120s cooldown at rank 1, easy to sidestep, and Prismatic Barrier covers what does land. Keep denying his stacks — enough Stardust upgrades it into The Skies Descend, and every level you keep him behind delays that.

notes: Kit-flag conflict: Aurelion Sol's Astral Flight (W) carries a 'terrain' derived flag, but Riot's own description says he flies OVER terrain — it does not create terrain. Per the brief's rule I trusted the description and did NOT write the _missing-interactions 'terrain-cuts-retreat' headline, which is built on that misfiring flag. Singularity's execute threshold percentage is not in Riot's text, so I wrote 'a percent threshold' rather than a number. breakdown.wave was judged templated (generic 'mid waves are bus tickets' phrasing reusable against any enemy) but I could not ground a replacement in this enemy's kit within the length band, so it was left alone. Chart group: phases[3..5].side moved Skill->Lux with matching why rewrites; win[3..5] already read 'Lux' so no content edits were proposed there (no-op would be rejected and would take the group down).
